title: Reject duplicate queries
task: A plan with the same query twice wastes a search. Make plan_queries treat duplicates (ignoring case and extra spaces) as an invalid reply, so the model gets one retry with the reason.
hint: Compare " ".join(q.lower().split()) for each query, and raise ValueError like the other checks so the except branch sends the reason back.

title: Cap query length
task: Queries longer than 80 characters are usually the question pasted back, and make poor searches. Treat them as invalid too.
hint: One more check before return queries: raise ValueError("query over 80 characters").

title: Add an age filter
task: Give search_places an optional integer argument age. Declare it in the schema, validate it in handle_tool_call (a whole number from 0 to 17), and drop places whose min_age is above it. An invalid age must not run the tool.
hint: In Python, True is an int, so check isinstance(x, int) and not isinstance(x, bool). Filter the list the tool returns rather than changing places.py.

title: Reject stopword-only queries
task: A query like "the of and" passes the empty-string check but cannot match anything. Reject it with invalid_arguments before the tool runs.
hint: places.terms(query) returns the searchable words. An empty list means there are none.

title: Refuse repeated searches
task: If the model proposes a search it already ran in this run, return an error with code duplicate_search instead of running the tool again.
hint: Keep a set of normalised queries inside run_agent and check it before calling handle_tool_call.

title: Add a context budget
task: Give run_agent a max_chars argument (default 20000). Before each model call, if the messages serialised as JSON are longer than that, stop with stop="context_budget".
hint: len(json.dumps(messages)) is a fine stand-in for tokens here. Return the same keys as the other stops.

title: Teach the judge about overclaiming
task: Make overlap_judge agree with all twelve hand labels in judge_labels.jsonl. Right now it passes two overstatements.
hint: Words like best, largest, only, all and every make a claim stronger than its vocabulary suggests. If the claim uses one that the summary does not, call it unsupported.

title: Check the expected places
task: Write cites_expected(claims, expect_any): True when at least one claim cites a place listed in expect_any. Use it in evaluate() to flag questions whose answer misses every expected place.
hint: any(c["cites"] in expect_any for c in claims)
